reviews.title: WARNING: $119.99 CHARGED IMMEDIATELY - NO FREE TRIAL
reviews.text:
This app is incredibly misleading. When prompted to subscribe to unlock all features, it explicitly advertises a 7-day free trial, yet I was charged $119.99 IMMEDIATELY without receiving the trial I was led to believe I was signing up for.

Let me be clear: ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY DOLLARS. Not $5. Not $10. Nearly $120 taken immediately when the app advertised a free trial.

I immediately canceled the subscription as soon as I discovered the charge and made three attempts to obtain a refund through Apple. My refund was denied three times despite the circumstances, leaving me with no choice but to dispute the charge directly with my bank.

It is absolutely unacceptable to advertise a 7-day free trial and then charge someone nearly $120 upfront. The fact that I canceled immediately and still couldn’t get my money back through Apple’s refund process makes this experience even  worse.

PLEASE BE CAREFUL BEFORE SUBSCRIBING. Read every detail, double-check the payment terms, and do not assume that selecting a 7-day free trial means you won’t be charged immediately. I would never have agreed to pay $119.99 upfront, and I want other users to be aware of what happened to me before they make the same mistake.

UPDATE/RESPONSE:

Thank you for responding, but I feel that your response avoids addressing the actual issue.

Your app explicitly displays “7-day free trial” directly above the subscribe button. This is exactly what I was presented with when prompted to subscribe to unlock all fea

reviews.title: Very disappointing experience with Planner 5D.
reviews.text:
I signed up believing I was starting a 7-day free trial, but instead I was charged $119.99 for an annual subscription immediately. As soon as I saw the charge, I canceled the subscription the same day.

What made the experience even worse was the difficulty getting a refund. I tried to resolve the issue through Apple and PayPal and ultimately had to dispute the charge with my bank.

I originally wanted to use Planner 5D to design my new home, but this billing experience completely changed my opinion of the service.

My advice: be extremely careful when signing up for a trial and check exactly when you will be charged before confirming anything.

UPDATE: Planner 5D responded to my review and asked me to contact their support team and request escalation to a senior team member. I followed their instructions. Their support asked for a screenshot of my Apple subscription, which I provided, but ultimately told me they could not help and directed me back to Apple, where my refund request had already been denied. I also now see other App Store reviews describing the same issue — agreeing to a trial and then being charged around $120. Unfortunately, my issue remains unresolved.

reviews.text: I tried scanning 3-4 times with an iPhone 16 Pro Max (with enough RAM and storage), and after 6-8 minutes (despite having bright lights, holding the phone steady and always vertical, clear home structure being scanned, moving slowly, and more), the app says all of a sudden says it was unable to save the scan. Other apps I've tried (coincidentally some at a fraction of the cost) never tend to have this issue (and I scanned with them the same day after trying this app and they did them successfully) and offer better services for my renovation needs once those scans are complete. This app may 100% be fantastic after a successful scan. And it could just be a buggy version when I installed this today. But unfortunately, it failed me at the scan itself and thus could not benefit from its services (e.g., renovation) on my the scan. I'm glad it offered a free trial as this was a flaw which hopefully can be fixed.

reviews.title: Such a waste of money
reviews.text:
I genuinely cannot believe people recommend Planner 5D with a straight face.

This app is marketed like some powerful interior design platform where you can realistically recreate your apartment and experiment with layouts, materials, colors, lighting, furniture, etc.

What it actually is:
a clunky, overpriced furniture-dragging simulator with the depth of a mobile game from 2014.

After spending over $100, I expected professional-level customization or at least a remotely convincing design experience. Instead I got generic furniture blocks that barely resemble real furniture, limited customization, awkward controls, and a fake-looking 3D environment that makes everything feel like a low-budget Sims knockoff.

Want to accurately match your real apartment?
Good luck.

Want to customize colors and materials in a meaningful way?
Prepare for disappointment.

Want your actual furniture to look remotely correct?
Not happening.

The entire experience becomes an endless cycle of:
drag object → resize object → rotate object → realize it still looks nothing like your room.

Yes, technically you can test rough spacing and layouts. But that is an insane amount of money to spend for what ultimately amounts to digital furniture Tetris.

Honestly, a tape measure, your phone camera, and common sense would get most people 80% of the way there with far less frustration.

This feels less like professional design software and more like an app built by people who are very good at marketing subscr

reviews.title: Lack of state management makes this unusable
reviews.text:
After carefully measuring my room and furniture to lay it out in the app, I succumbed to the temptation to use the “Bernard AI” features. In addition to producing an incoherent design, it broke my floor plan (disconnecting walls, etc) and deleted my furniture—perhaps as expected. What I didn’t expect is an inability to restore any of the work I had previously done. This is apparently a known issue, affecting not just AI changes but any attempts to revert to older versions. This seemingly makes it impossible to experiment with different arrangements, ie use the software for its intended purpose.

The help robot and a very nice customer service person suggested duplicating often as a workaround, a very helpful suggestion arriving way too late. This workflow is not part of the New User Experience and the duplicate button is not anywhere on the actual editing screen on iOS.

I’m genuinely shocked to have lost the work and hope my subscription will be refunded.

The programming for this app is so unbelievably bad, I couldn’t imaging paying more than 3 cents for the features hidden behind an overpriced paywall. Overall it’s really not too bad for an ios app, but when you start to get into the specifics of things it starts to get quite a bit ridiculous and infuriating to say the least. Fix the glitches, fix the dimensions and it would be golden, even on the free plan.

So you try to do it manually and the app itself has no ideal way to place doors windows or objects at exact distance from walls etc. 
It seems like it tried to "override" permissions to help but ends up doing nothing but waste your time.

Trying to create rooms from scratch is a total nightmare. From "Sketch" it does not allow you to edit measurements you do it by moving your finger across the screen. And after minutes of trying to get a single line to a desired measurement, making the next line literally changes the previous lines dimensions. It has no ability to render exterior from existing images apparently only kitchen, rooms and restrooms. 
I payed for the whole year subscription and it is absolutely useless! I can't imagine how much worse the "free" version is. Even worse! The $400 supposed premium package? This app is absolutely trash. (Unless the developers fix absolutely every aspect of it.)

reviews.title: Not good

Scam! Just want to take your money! I strongly warn others before signing up for the Planner 5D free trial.

During the trial, the app was unusable on both my phone and computer due to multiple defects and missing core functionality. Because of this, I attempted to cancel before the trial ended. I clearly remember initiating cancellation, but I received no confirmation.

Despite this, the trial was automatically converted into a £119.99 annual charge.

I contacted  Apple and was denied a refund due to the developer’s policy. Charging a large annual fee for a defective product, especially after an attempted cancellation and without clear confirmation, feels deeply misleading.
